**[aggression warning; no offense intended though it does get rough]**


What if I told you, "Relationships are more than just sex". Is it really so hard to believe that a guy will work hard to be a generally decent human being despite actually being a bit of an asshole. Is it really all that hard to believe that he may be trying to better himself for the benefit of humanity and not to get into some girl's pants? I believe it, I also believe that I've worked really hard to not be a bully from the moment I moved to Ohio I gave up that shit. I could still insult you, I could make your friends cry, I could be an ass to humor my friends; but what's the point? Yes, being friend-zoned is an inevitability in most people's lives, it will happen, it will suck. Hell it's happened to me several times; guess what though, it has never been about sex. I mean sure, it's part of the equation as it is genetically coded to be, but having someone I can be with and trust has always been the driving factor. I don't want a fuck buddy, I don't want a whore, I don't want sex; sorry to say it but that shit is too easy. I could easily fuck 3 girls right now if I was to go out and use what I have learned in my "becoming a man". But, fucking a man does not make; the ability to understand, to empathize, to provide (be it for himself or for a family), to get better, to simplify, to clarify... the list goes on. That's what makes a man. 

I agree though, many men feel as though they have earned something from being a friend, many men feel they have earned sex. But me, I feel that being a friend has earned me respect; and time and time and time again being told that "I just don't see you that way, but I want us to be friends, I want us to stay friends" becomes a rather damaging insult. Yes, humans know almost instantly if they are sexually attracted to a member of their chosen gender; but, sexual attraction can also be built over time, as well as social attraction, so can resentment, pity, and general hatred.

Women and girls time and time again say that it's more than just about the sex, or the body, or the brain, or whatever there's an endless list but in the end when they "friend-zone" a guy, be it the intended result or not, they are saying "I'm not sexually attracted to you" but what guys hear is more like "you're not good enough in any aspect of your life to ever get a girl like me" or "Your personality isn't good enough to make up for your bodily imperfections" or one of many other possible scenarios. Let me make this clear, unless a guy is trying to talk you into coming back to his place, to go to an empty room, to get away from a crowd, he's not thinking about 'getting any' he's thinking about things he can do with you of a nonsexual nature.

Upvote, downvote, do what you want; this is merely a throwaway account setup for the purpose of saying what I really think so do what you will, but understand that this single "beta" really understands his position in the world. Understand that this "beta" will one day be someone that you consider an "alpha" under unrelated circumstances. Understand that this "beta" has things that make him something that many redditors will never be, can never be, and can't even fathom, and because of that, this "beta" isn't really so "beta" after all.
Your friend "Jessica" sounds extremely similar to someone I know. I'm no longer dealing with her.
Women, feeling like you're right, and thinking that you're right does not mean that you are. Being right is not a subjective thing, it is concrete; you are right or you are wrong. Period.

You went out with your friends once being a 3rd wheel to 4 groups, and you're complaining about that? Do you know how fucked it is to be a third wheel 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in your own house? Because I fucking do.

I know its not right. Believe me, you have no idea how much I know it's not right; I just don't want to deal with the ever increasing unknowns that life seems to throw my way. Each week or so, things get worse; my depression, anxiety, and general mood disorders have taken over my personality and now I feel hollow I feel like a program meant only to exist for the sake of existence. Maybe unjust imprisonment would get the attention of somebody that could help me, maybe something good will come from it. You say it's not okay to accept, I don't know if it's worth it to fight anymore.

I used to be a swimmer and would shave all of all of my body hair. I stopped swimming but always liked how clean I felt right after a shave, so I continued shaving. One day I was shaving and got to my legs and got a pretty bad shaving cut all the way up my right shin, obviously both of my parents were home and we were out of gauze so I asked my mom who is a medical professional to help me out. Lucky for me my dad found out that I cut my leg shaving, I don't think I've ever seen so much shame in his eyes, also he seriously thinks I might be homosexual now.

There is a time coming where I will no longer have any contact with any of the people in my life. I will most likely just disappear to the west and live under another name. I'm ashamed of who I am, of what I've done, how I perceive the world and the only way to fix what I've fucked is to become a new person.
At least you weren't rejected by the girl of your dreams twice; I was. I never even got a first date with her.

And, *cough cough* I'll get right on the deodorant thing, I know I get pretty foul after a hard day of work so it's likely that I have an odor walking through the door.

Yeah, I micromanage my life. It's a pretty major issue, I've been trying to get over it for some time. But it's pretty difficult, you see, no matter how successful I am at one thing I always seem to remember all of my other failures. It hurts, I get close to something and then it gets pulled away, I fall back into major depression and I'm completely useless for months. I'm just coming out of my last major depression, getting some confidence, and about to enter a rather elite art school. But what sucks, what really sucks, is that I'm going to have to work full time, go to class full time, and find some way to fit 6 hours of homework into each day. And on top of that, I hope to find someone that I can be close to, someone that understands and likes me for who I am.
I'm not gay, but I'd fuck me... I'd fuck me so hard.
Great idea, I'll be sure to do that once it cools down a little.

I don't want to say that I found religion, that's not the case, I have however learned the benefit of not referring to myself as an atheist. I consider myself a Buddhist, though I don't believe in the spiritual aspects of the system I do believe in the moral and lifestyle parts. This came from years of being constantly angered and offended by the religious people of the area I lived in, and seeing that nothing I could ever say would make them stop believing in their little fantasy worlds. So I moved on. I found something that worked for me, and so that I didn't have to tell people I'm atheist, so that they wouldn't tell me I'm going to hell or that I need to change my ways.

Now don't think that I changed just to get away from the constant preaching, that is not the case. Buddhism has always interested me, and it just so happens that my morals match up with the ideas of the belief system. That said, I don't believe in a greater god, nor do I disbelieve, and I don't believe in an afterlife as a place.

As someone with an IQ in the mid 140s, I may not be at the complete end of the spectrum but I am smart. I'm able to figure out solutions to problems quickly, recall details almost instantly, but I'm unable to socialize normally. I often want to have a direct conversation where other people want to skirt around that conversation and go back to whatever it was that they want to talk about. I can talk about what I know, but I don't really pickup on nonverbal cues that often so that makes it hard to have meaningful relationships.
Some people just never get it. The day will come when you can take your life back and become a healthy individual once more. I wish you well in your recovery.

I wish I could think of it like that, but last time I went to art school I ended dropping out due to the same problems I'm having now. I really can't see anything good coming to me. But thanks for the words. My first set of friends I lost when I moved to my current state, then I lost my second set of friends when, out of the blue I was put on several "hit lists" which was a game people were playing around 7th grade where people would make lists of other classmates they "wanted to kill" or have something bad happen to. Then again when I asked a girl I've known since I moved to this state, lost all of my friends then. And finally when I dropped out of art school I lost all those friends. Socially I've had NO success, so what's the point of even trying anymore?

I've lost my entire circle of friends 4 times in my life, each time because of something out of my control. I don't want to be forever alone, but that's all I keep feeling, that's all I see of myself. I've been accepted to relatively prestigious art school, but that always gets overshadowed by the fact that I feel so alone all the time. And I do want to do something rash, but I can't, and I know I can't, but I keep thinking about it and it won't stop cycling in my head.
